_comment: Every entry is one insiliscope_cli run (options as in `insiliscope_cli --help`, without the leading --) rendered to a GIF. Adding a feature = adding an entry and placing it in a row of 'sections' (the page: a story per section, rows of side-by-side panels; build_gallery.py refuses an entry no row shows).
_paint: DNA-PAINT in the gallery (defaults and the overview's sr): every imager at a tenth of its cli default and bound 10x longer, so about as many imagers are bound per frame (k_on c t_on is the same) over a tenth of the free-imager background.
_bf: The brightfield entries are 512 px wide: their phase contrast is weak against the camera noise, and a wide field shown at panel size averages the noise down and shows whole cells.
_overview: The 2x2 overview at the top of the gallery and on the Home page (tools/build_overview.py): one spot (x, y, um; tools/build_overview.py --suggest), its map, structures, widefield and SMLM movies.
_sections: The gallery page: per section a story and rows of side-by-side panels (an entry id, or [id, label]); shared: one display range for the row.
_defaults: Every movie looks at the same spot (x, y; chosen 2026-10-15: about 75% of a nucleus in the top-left corner, the microtubules spreading out to the cell edge, an empty strip in the bottom-right corner).

entries.title: Default SMLM movie
entries.text: The default CellField, two targets at once: the microtubules in DNA-PAINT with an ATTO 655 imager (0.1 nM, bound 0.5 s; 640 nm) on 70% of their binding sites through primary + secondary antibodies (IgG2-PAINT), and the nuclear pores (8 per um^2 of envelope, Nup96-SNAP) in DNA-PAINT with a Cy3B imager (0.25 nM, bound 0.5 s; 561 nm) on 60% of their sites (the gallery's imagers are a tenth of the defaults, 1 and 2.5 nM, bound ten times longer than the default 50 ms: about as many bound per frame, a tenth of the free-imager background), both lasers through a multi-band filter set (light-preset auto); the free imagers' background under a HILO sheet (the DNA-PAINT presets' illum-bfp 0.95), the Gibson-Lanni + Zernike PSF (MixedRealisticObjective aberrations), Kinetix22 sCMOS noise; 60 s after the illumination came on.

entries.title: Dense activation
entries.text: The microtubules' imager at 1.43 nM (the gallery's default is 0.1 nM): ~14 times the binding rate, overlapping emitters and a ~14 times brighter free-imager background.

entries.title: Very dense: binned blinks (approximate SMLM)
entries.text: Imager 10 nM: over 12.5 ON blinks per um^2 (~130), so every frame renders binned (blink-binned-density-per-um2 12.5): the same blinks snapped to a grid of 2 cells per pixel (+-25 nm) and FFT-convolved per PSF plane, at a cost per field of view instead of per blink.

entries.title: Very dense: blinks mean-field
entries.text: The same 10 nM movie with blink-mean-field-max-emitters 0: no blinks drawn, each dye's expected ON time x the dye density, convolved once. The total signal is right, but the blinking is gone (only shot noise is left), so this is not SMLM data; off by default.

entries.title: dSTORM, AF647
entries.text: mt-dye AF647 (its dSTORM mode, 3% of the sites) with its light preset (dSTORM-640): blinks with Dempsey et al.'s photons per cycle and duty cycle, scaled to the laser intensity.

entries.title: dSTORM, the first seconds
entries.text: The same from t = 0 (start-sec 0): every dye starts ON and switches off over its initial ON time, so the movie starts as a widefield image and turns into blinks.

entries.title: PALM, mEos3.2
entries.text: mt-dye mEos3.2 (PALM, 25% of the sites) with its 561 nm preset (405 nm at 2 W/cm²): photoconverted proteins blink red until they bleach.

entries.title: PALM, mEos3.2 green state
entries.text: mEos3.2 imaged through the 488 nm path (WF-488 light preset) from t = 0: the unconverted green state shows as a widefield image, the red blinks barely pass the green filter.

entries.title: Constant brightness, bright blinks
entries.text: The microtubules alone (npc-dye None) at 4 kW/cm^2 of 640 nm (laser-640 4, the default 1), so the blinks are bright, with the dye field photon-cv set to 0 (mt-dye.photon-cv): every blink equally bright (the library's is 0.5, a log-normal per-blink brightness spread with mean 1).

entries.title: DNA-PAINT without the imager background
entries.text: The default movie with the free-imager background left out (chamber-height-um 0): only the bound imagers. The background is the imager in the illuminated chamber; its depletion and its exclusion from cells are ignored.

entries.title: Background
entries.text: 50 background photons per pixel per second on top of the default movie.

entries.title: Sample drift (random walk)
entries.text: drift-xy-nm-per-sqrt-sec 200, drift-z-nm-per-sqrt-sec 100: a normal step per frame and axis, summed (RMS 200 nm per axis after 1 s; a stable setup drifts ~5-20). Exaggerated so it shows in 3 s; the cli also writes the true drift per frame (.drift.csv).

entries.title: Directed drift
entries.text: drift-xy-speed-nm-per-sec 600 in a seed-drawn direction swinging within +/-20 deg, drift-z-speed-nm-per-sec 150 upwards (drift-z-direction 1) swinging between full speed and still (the default 90 deg z wander), 30% speed wander (correlation time 1 s here, 60 s by default) and a little random walk (20 nm/sqrt(s)). Exaggerated so it shows in 3 s.

entries.title: Fiducial beads under drift
entries.text: The random-walk drift of the panel before (drift-xy-nm-per-sqrt-sec 200, drift-z-nm-per-sqrt-sec 100) with 100 nm gold nanoparticles on the coverslip (fid-type Gold, fid-density 0.03 per um^2: 7 beads here). Gold does not bleach or blink: its photoluminescence (about 80000 detected photons/s per bead here, after Balinovic et al. 2019) plus a little scattered laser light that leaks through the filters. The beads move with the sample, so their positions over the movie are the drift the .drift.csv records.

entries.title: Focus 2 um above the coverslip
entries.text: Z stage at 2 um: dyes near the focal plane are sharp, those above and below it blur with the 3D PSF.

entries.title: Low NA (0.9)
entries.text: A wider PSF at NA 0.9 (diffraction limit about 0.61 lambda / NA).

entries.title: High NA (1.49)
entries.text: The same field at NA 1.49.

entries.title: Gaussian PSF (for comparison)
entries.text: psf-model Gaussian: sigma = 0.21 lambda / NA, no defocus, no aberrations. Fast, but every dye looks in focus.

entries.title: Strong astigmatism
entries.text: psf-zernike-preset AstigmatismStrong (Zernike j = 5) at the default focus: spots stretch along x or y with their height above or below the focal plane.

entries.title: Whole PSF kernel per blink
entries.text: psf-halo-cut 0 (as Renderer.Quality Exhaustive): every blink drawn with the whole +/-7 um kernel. The default (3e-6) leaves out pixels below 3 photons in a million of the emitter's; the difference is far below the noise.

entries.title: Every blink drawn, however dim
entries.text: blink-min-photons 0 (as Renderer.Quality Exhaustive): the blinks that give a frame fewer than 50 photons (the default, Realistic; Fast: 100) are drawn too, mostly those that only start or end in the frame.

entries.title: Nearest-grid placement
entries.text: psf-interp Nearest: each emitter snaps to the 1/6 px kernel grid instead of the default cubic interpolation at its true position.

entries.title: Index mismatch (widefield)
entries.text: psf-sample-index 1.33 (water) with emitters 3 um deep (psf-sample-depth-nm 3000): Gibson-Lanni spherical aberration and focal shift; defocus blurs less in the lower-index sample. Same focus position as the matched-index movie (z 0.5 um).

entries.title: Noisy camera
entries.text: Read noise 6 e-, a flat QE of 0.5 (qe-curve Custom), 10% pixel-to-pixel gain spread.

entries.title: EMCCD camera
entries.text: camera-preset iXonUltra897 (EMCCD gain register: excess noise, its read noise, CIC and QE curve) at EM gain ~20 (gain 0.05 e-/ADU, about 20 ADU per photoelectron): at the preset's single-molecule setting (0.0066 e-/ADU, EM gain ~150) the DNA-PAINT background fills the 16-bit range and every pixel saturates.

entries.title: Widefield, mEGFP
entries.text: mt-dye mEGFP (WideField mode, 70% of the sites) with its 488 nm preset: every dye emits at once, mean-field 3D PSF convolution over world-anchored z planes.

entries.title: Widefield photobleaching
entries.text: mEGFP with a 2000-photon budget (mt-dye.photon-budget) and 500 ms frames from t = 0: the image fades with the exact per-frame bleaching integral.

entries.title: Crosstalk: mEGFP in the 561 nm channel
entries.text: mEGFP imaged through the WF-561 light path: the residual 561 nm excitation and the red tail of its emission give a faint image (detected fraction and rate: Fluorophores.Microtubules_DetectedPct / PhotonsPerSecOn in MM).

entries.title: Widefield, focus 2 um up
entries.text: Focus moved up through the sample: the coverslip structures blur, upper cell features sharpen.

entries.title: Widefield focus sweep
entries.text: The focus moves from the coverslip to 4 um above it and back in 0.25 um steps, one frame per height (z_sweep; every dye in the cell counts: z-range-um 0): the coverslip structures blur as the upper cell features sharpen.

entries.title: Brightfield, focus 0.5 um
entries.text: Transmitted light through the cells' refractive index (cytoplasm, nucleus, microtubules only), partially coherent multislice optics at the default quality 3: near focus a phase object shows little contrast.

entries.title: Brightfield, focus 2 um below the coverslip
entries.text: z = -2: defocus turns the cells' phase into intensity; the nucleus dome acts as a weak lens and shows bright.

entries.title: Brightfield focus sweep
entries.text: The focus moves from 2 um below the coverslip to 2 um above it and back in 0.25 um steps, one frame per height (z_sweep): the cells, weak phase objects, are faint in focus and change contrast sign through it.

entries.title: Brightfield, nearly coherent
entries.text: bf-condenser-na 0.1: a closed condenser makes edges ring and raises contrast (fewer angles average out).

entries.title: Brightfield, plain ellipsoid nuclei
entries.text: p.nucIrregMin/Max 0, p.nucBendMax 0, p.nucThickIrreg 0, p.nucAsym 0, p.nucWidestMin/Max 0.5: the nucleus shape switched off (lobes, kidney bend, uneven thickness, wider base), for comparison with the default.

entries.title: Brightfield, quality 1 (fastest)
entries.text: bf-quality 1: one thin phase screen, 6 condenser points, camera-pixel grid; compare with the default (quality 3).

entries.title: Lasers and lamp both on
entries.text: light-epi 1 and light-trans 1: the DNA-PAINT fluorescence and a dimmed lamp (5000 photons/px/s) on one camera, the lamp's photons times the QE added before one noise chain.

entries.title: Cell packing off
entries.text: Packing disabled: cells may overlap (the packing step is what makes the layout chaotic and seed-exact).

entries.title: Higher occupancy, denser microtubules
entries.text: Occupancy 0.5, microtubule density 1.6 per um^2.

entries.title: Widefield nanorulers
entries.text: Every docking strand's ATTO 655 emitting at once (ruler-mode WideField): diffraction-limited spots, one per rod.

entries.title: 2D origami: TU Delft logos, 320 nm spacing
entries.text: origami-design TUDelftLogo: flat DNA origami lying face up at random angles, each with one docking strand on each of 37 hexagons of the TU Delft logo. At origami-spacing-nm 320 the strands sit 320 nm apart, wider than the PSF, so in WideField (every strand's ATTO 655 at once, from the first second: start-sec 0, before they bleach) the logo is readable without super-resolution; at the default 80 nm it is one blur. The 640 nm laser at 0.1 kW/cm^2 (laser-640 0.1, 10x the WF-640 preset) for bright spots.

entries.title: Microtubules alone
entries.text: The default movie with the nuclear pores unlabelled (npc-dye None): the microtubules in DNA-PAINT with ATTO 655 at 640 nm.

entries.title: Nuclear pores alone
entries.text: The default movie with the microtubules unlabelled (mt-dye None): the pores in DNA-PAINT with Cy3B at 561 nm, focus 0.85 um up, where this nucleus starts (its lowest pores lie at 0.8 um).

entries.title: Bright blinks
entries.text: The microtubules alone (npc-dye None) at 4 kW/cm^2 of 640 nm (laser-640 4, the default 1): about four times the photons per blink, with the library's brightness spread (photon-cv 0.5).

entries.title: Strong spherical aberration
entries.text: psf-zernike-preset SphericalStrong (primary spherical aberration, Zernike j = 12), the strongest spherical preset, in place of the default MixedRealisticObjective.

entries.title: Microtubules, ground truth
entries.text: The microtubules of the field of view as the world model places them (coloured by height in the viewer's scale: blue at the coverslip, white at the top of the cell), over the cell and its nucleus.

entries.title: Nuclear pores, ground truth
entries.text: The nuclear pores of the field of view, one dot each, coloured by height as in the viewer: red on the lower envelope facing the coverslip, light yellow on top.

entries.title: Both targets, ground truth
entries.text: Microtubules and nuclear pores together.

entries.title: DNA-PAINT nanorulers, TIRF
entries.text: specimen Nanorulers: DNA-origami rods on the coverslip, three spots of five docking strands 80 nm apart, the ATTO 655 imager at 2 nM bound 2.9 s (a tenth of the default 20 nM, ten times its bound time), 100 ms frames, in TIRF (the nanorulers' light preset, illum-bfp 1.03): an evanescent layer about 150 nm deep lights the strands and only the imager near the coverslip.

entries.title: DNA-PAINT nanorulers, HILO
entries.text: The same in HILO (illum-bfp 0.95): an inclined sheet a few um thick lights the imager above the strands too.

entries.title: DNA-PAINT nanorulers, epi
entries.text: The same in epi (illum-bfp 0): the imager in the whole lit column raises the background about ninefold.

entries.title: Epi illumination
entries.text: illum-bfp 0: the laser spot at the centre of the back focal plane, the beam straight up through the sample. The default DNA-PAINT movie is HILO (0.95); in epi the free imager in the whole lit column adds its background.

entries.title: TIRF
entries.text: illum-bfp 1.03: past the critical angle, an evanescent layer about 150 nm deep (at 640 nm). The free-imager background drops, and the microtubules above the layer go dark: only those near the coverslip are lit.

entries.title: Flat beam profile
entries.text: illum-profile Flat: a laterally infinite beam instead of the default Gaussian (FWHM 100 % of the field's width, a quarter of the centre's light in the corners): the corners are as bright as the centre.

entries.title: FlatTop beam profile
entries.text: illum-profile FlatTop: a disc with a soft edge (the logistic edge of the SMLM Challenge simulator), FWHM 100 % of the field's width, instead of the default Gaussian: even over most of the field, dimmer only in the corners.

sections.title: One sample, three microscopes
sections.story: Every movie on this page looks at the same spot of an endless field of synthetic cells (seed 42): a nucleus in the top-left corner, microtubules spreading out to the cell's edge, and a strip of empty coverslip in the bottom-right corner, through a 128 x 128 pixel camera with 100 nm pixels. The sample never changes; the microscope does. Here it is imaged three ways: single molecules blinking in DNA-PAINT, a fluorescent protein in widefield, and the unlabelled cells in transmitted light.

rows.caption: Same place, same cells (brightfield over a 4x wider field, 512 px, centred on the same spot). SMLM sees the molecules that happen to be on in each frame, widefield every dye at once, brightfield only the refractive index of the cells.

sections.title: How single molecules blink
sections.story: Super-resolution needs molecules that are dark most of the time and light up one by one. Three chemistries do that, and each has its own rhythm. dSTORM dyes start bright and are pumped into a dark state they leave rarely; PALM proteins are switched on by violet light and bleach after one burst; DNA-PAINT imagers bind and unbind for ever.

rows.caption: The microtubules in the three modes, each with its typical dye and lasers, a minute into the acquisition.
Time matters. dSTORM starts as a widefield image and breaks up into blinks; unconverted mEos3.2 glows green before any of it is converted.
Real blinks vary in brightness (a log-normal spread); switching that off makes every spot alike. Bright blinks (4 kW/cm<sup>2</sup> at 640 nm) on the microtubules alone.

sections.title: From sparse to dense
sections.story: Turn up the DNA-PAINT imager and more molecules are bound at once. At some point the spots overlap and SMLM stops working; the simulation goes along and switches how it draws the blinks, so even a crowded frame renders quickly. The last panel shows why the mean-field shortcut is off by default: the brightness is right, the blinking is gone.

rows.caption: The microtubules' imager concentration from 0.1 to 10 nM (bound 0.5 s). Binned: the same blinks on a finer grid, one convolution per frame. Mean field: no blinks at all, only their average.

sections.title: What else reaches the camera
sections.story: A real SMLM frame is never just molecules. In DNA-PAINT the free imager in the buffer glows everywhere, autofluorescence adds more, and the sample creeps while you record. Each can be switched on and off on its own.

rows.caption: Each source of background adds to the last.
Drift, exaggerated to show in 3 s: a random walk, and a fast creep (600 nm/s) whose direction swings. The cli writes the true path next to the movie; fiducial beads on the sample follow it.

sections.title: Two targets in one cell
sections.story: The cell field carries two labelled structures at once: the microtubules and the nuclear pores, each with its own dye, mode and laser. The top row is what is really there, the bottom row what the camera makes of it. The pores sit on the nuclear envelope, so for the pores alone the focus goes up to where the nucleus starts (0.85 um).

rows.caption: The world model's positions in this field of view, in the viewer's colours (height above the coverslip).
Two colours, one camera: ATTO 655 on the microtubules, Cy3B on the pores, through a multi-band filter set. In the two-target movie the dense microtubules outshine most pores.

sections.title: Focus and the objective
sections.story: The cells are a few micrometres tall and the focus is a plane through them. What lies above or below it blurs with the 3D PSF; the objective's numerical aperture sets how small a spot can get.

rows.caption: Moving the focus up: the microtubules on the coverslip blur, the top of the cell comes in.
Focus sweeps, one frame per 0.25 um. In brightfield the cells are nearly invisible in focus and change contrast through it.
A higher NA collects more light into a smaller spot.

sections.title: How the light reaches the sample
sections.story: Where the laser spot sits in the objective's back focal plane decides the light's path: in its centre the beam goes straight up (epi), towards the edge it leaves at a slant as a thin sheet (HILO), past the critical angle it is reflected and only an evanescent layer reaches the cells (TIRF). The beam is a Gaussian as wide as the field by default.

rows.caption: Epi lights the free imager through the whole chamber, HILO only a sheet, TIRF only the first ~150 nm: the background falls, and in TIRF the microtubules higher in the cell go dark.
A Gaussian beam dims steadily towards the edges, a flat-top one only in the corners; a flat one lights the field evenly.

sections.title: Shaping the PSF
sections.story: The default PSF is a Gibson-Lanni model with Zernike aberrations of a realistic objective. Aberrations can be dialled in on purpose: astigmatism makes spots stretch with their height, which is how 3D SMLM works.

rows.caption: A Gaussian looks in focus everywhere; the diffraction model does not. All four at the same focus (0.5 um).
Imaging into water with an oil objective adds spherical aberration and shifts the focus. Both movies are taken at the same focus position (z = 0.5 um).

sections.title: The camera
sections.story: The photons become electrons and counts in a camera model: shot noise, read noise, pixel-to-pixel spreads, and for an EMCCD the gain register's extra noise.

rows.caption: The same movie on three cameras. The EMCCD runs at a low EM gain: at its single-molecule setting the DNA-PAINT background saturates every pixel.

sections.title: Widefield: every dye at once
sections.story: In widefield every dye emits at the same time, so the simulation convolves the whole dye density with the 3D PSF instead of placing molecules one by one. Dyes bleach as they use up their photons, and colours leak into neighbouring channels.

rows.caption: Crosstalk: the green protein still shows faintly through the orange filter set (each panel on its own display range).
Photobleaching over 20 s with a small photon budget per dye.

sections.title: Brightfield: contrast from refractive index
sections.story: Without any dye, the light that passes through the cells is bent by their refractive index. These movies cover 51 um (512 px) so whole cells show. Only the structures the simulation knows about (cytoplasm, nucleus, microtubules) make contrast; the optics are a partially coherent multislice model.

rows.caption: In focus a phase object barely shows; defocus or a closed condenser turns phase into contrast.
The nucleus shape matters; the fastest quality level is a single phase screen.
Both light sources on one camera: the fluorescence on top of a dimmed brightfield image.

sections.title: The world behind it
sections.story: The cells are placed by a packing step that keeps them from overlapping; occupancy and microtubule density are parameters of the world, not of the microscope.

rows.caption: Three worlds in widefield.

sections.title: DNA-origami nanorulers
sections.story: The second sample: DNA-origami rods on the coverslip, each with three spots of docking strands 80 nm apart, or flat origami in any design. A standard for testing resolution.

rows.caption: The three spots of a rod fall within one pixel; only the localisations resolve them. The deeper the light reaches into the imager solution, the brighter its background.
In widefield every strand glows at once: one diffraction-limited spot per rod. Flat origami with the strands spread wider than the PSF: the logo reads without super-resolution.

sections.title: Render quality
sections.story: A few switches trade accuracy for speed. At the defaults the difference should be invisible under the noise; that is how the defaults were chosen. Each panel is one of those switches turned all the way up (or down), with the time it takes per frame (this machine's cli, measured when the gallery was built).

rows.caption: Four ways of drawing the same blinks.
